messages.content: How can I sell my acoustic guitar?

function.name: tune_instrument
function.description: This function helps tune instruments based on the instrument type and the desired key or note. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

instrument_type.description: The type of the instrument, e.g. 'acoustic guitar', 'piano'.

key.description: The key or note to which the instrument should be tuned to. Default is 'Standard' for guitars.

message.content:
Here’s a quick, step‑by‑step guide to help you get your acoustic guitar sold quickly and safely: | Step | What to Do | Why It Matters | |------|------------|----------------| | **1. Clean & Tune** | Give the guitar a thorough cleaning (strings, fretboard, body). Tune it to standard pitch. | A well‑presented instrument looks more appealing and shows you’ve cared for it. | | **2. Take Quality Photos** | Capture the whole body, headstock, strings, fretboard, and any imperfections. Use natural light and a neutral background. | Good photos attract buyers and reduce the chance of disputes over condition. | | **3. Research Market Value** | Check recent sales on Reverb, eBay, Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, and local classifieds. Note price ranges for similar models, ages, and conditions. | Helps you set a realistic price and avoid underselling. | | **4. Write a Clear Listing** | Include:
• Brand & model
• Age (if known)
• Condition (new, like new, used, etc.)
• Any upgrades or repairs
• Reason for selling
• Shipping options (if any)
• Payment methods | Transparency builds trust and speeds up negotiations. | | **5. Choose Your Platforms** | • **Reverb** – great for musical instruments, buyer protection.
• **eBay** – broad audience, auction or fixed price.
• **Craigslist / Facebook Marketplace** – local, no shipping needed.
• **Local music stores** – they may buy or consign.
• **Pawn shops** – quick cash, but usually lower offers. | Different platforms reach different buyer types; use a mix for best coverage. | | **6. Set a Competitive Price** | Start slightly above your target to allow room for negotiation. For example, if similar guitars sell for $300–$350, list yours at $375. | Buyers often expect to haggle; a higher starting point keeps you from selling too low. | | **7. Secure Payment** | • **Cash** – safest for local sales.
• **PayPal / Venmo** – offers buyer protection.
• **Escrow services** – for high‑value items. | Protects against fraud and ensures you receive funds before handing over the guitar. | | **8. Arrange Safe Delivery** | • Local: meet in a public place or at a police station.
• Shipping: use a tracked, insured service (UPS, FedEx, USPS Priority Mail). Pack the guitar in a hard case or padded box. | Reduces risk of theft or damage during transport. | | **9. Keep Records** | Save receipts, shipping labels, and any correspondence. | Useful for tax reporting and dispute resolution. | | **10. Follow Up** | Confirm receipt, ask for feedback, and thank the buyer. | Builds a good reputation if you plan to sell again. | ### Quick Tips - **Avoid “as‑is” listings** unless you’re sure the buyer will accept it; most buyers prefer a clean, tuned instrument. - **Offer a small discount** for buyers who pay immediately or bring the guitar in person. - **Use a reputable shipping carrier** with insurance; a $50–$100 loss is worth the extra cost. - **Check local regulations**: some states require a sales tax receipt for private sales. ### Example Listing (Reverb) ``` Title: 2008 Yamaha FG800 Acoustic Guitar – Excellent Condition Description: - Brand: Yamaha - Model: FG800 - Year: 2008 - Condition: Excellent (no scratches, no cracks) - Features: Solid spruce top, nato/okume back & sides, 25.5" scale - Reason for selling: Upgrading to a 12‑string - Shipping: Free, insured, tracked (UPS Ground) - Payment: PayPal (buyer protection) Photos: [Attach 5–7 images] Price: $375 (fixed) ``` Feel free to adapt this template to your specific guitar and platform. Good luck with your sale!
